name: AD — Object Security Descriptor Modified (DACL Backdoor)
description:
Attacker objective
Grant stealthy rights (DCSync/GenericAll/WriteDACL) on an AD object for persistence or escalation by modifying its security descriptor.

Attack logic
Security-descriptor changes on directory objects are normally system-driven (for example AdminSDHolder propagation under the SYSTEM context). Human-driven descriptor changes — especially on Tier-0 objects — can plant an ACL backdoor such as replication (DCSync) rights.

Why this detection works
Event 5136 records nTSecurityDescriptor modifications with the acting subject, so excluding SYSTEM isolates human-driven ACL changes.

False positives
Authorised delegation changes.

Tuning
Correlate with change control; pay special attention to grants of replication (DCSync), GenericAll or WriteDACL rights.

Required telemetry
Windows Security 5136 (AttributeLDAPDisplayName=nTSecurityDescriptor, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. SubjectUserName changed the ACL of ObjectDN.
2. Inspect the added ACE (DCSync / GenericAll / WriteDACL) and remove it if malicious; investigate the subject.
